# Chat/RAG Requirements Quality Checklist: P-RF04 — Interactive chat with memory (RAG)

**Purpose**: Pre-implementation requirements-quality review covering RF04's four main requirement clusters — streaming/failure/retry state machine, offline & connectivity behavior, side menu sessions (list/pagination/titling), and RAG grounding & persistence semantics — ahead of `/speckit-tasks`.
**Created**: 2026-10-19
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

## Requirement Completeness

- [ ] CHK001 Are requirements defined for an SSE connection that fails to establish at all (before `message_created`), as distinct from a mid-stream drop? [Gap, Spec §FR-004/FR-005]
- [ ] CHK002 Is the behavior specified for a retry request that itself returns an immediate non-streaming error (e.g., 4xx) before any streaming begins? [Gap, Spec §FR-006]
- [ ] CHK003 Are requirements defined for what the composer/UI shows between the user tapping send and the lazily-created session's `POST /chat/sessions` response arriving? [Gap, Spec §FR-010]
- [ ] CHK004 Is there a requirement for what the side menu shows while the first page of `GET /chat/sessions` is still loading (empty state vs. loading indicator)? [Gap, Spec §FR-008]
- [ ] CHK005 Are requirements defined for the local cache's retention limits (if any) across previously-opened conversations, or is unbounded retention an implicit assumption? [Gap, Spec §FR-011]
- [ ] CHK006 Is a requirement defined for the case where `POST /chat/sessions` succeeds but the following first-message send fails, leaving a session that exists with no messages? [Gap, Edge Cases]

## Requirement Clarity

- [ ] CHK007 Is "most recent activity" (`lastUserMessageAt`) ordering unambiguous for two sessions sharing an identical timestamp, so side-menu/pagination order is stable? [Clarity, Spec §FR-008]
- [ ] CHK008 Is the "short, trimmed preview" title-derivation rule (length, truncation boundary, whitespace handling) specified precisely enough for two implementers to produce identical output? [Clarity, Spec §FR-010, Assumptions]
- [ ] CHK009 Is "near the backend's maximum length" in the message-length edge case quantified with the actual numeric limit the client must enforce or detect? [Clarity, Edge Cases]
- [ ] CHK010 Is the "standard no-connection state" shown for a never-cached conversation (FR-011, Edge Cases) specified with enough detail to distinguish it from the offline banner shown over a cached conversation? [Clarity, Spec §FR-011]

## Requirement Consistency

- [ ] CHK011 Do FR-007 (single-flight gating per conversation) and FR-012 (block create/send/retry while offline) combine consistently for the case of being offline while a response is already in flight for that same conversation? [Consistency, Spec §FR-007/§FR-012]
- [ ] CHK012 Is the terminal-state vocabulary in FR-004 ("complete response" / "Falha ao gerar resposta") consistent with the Key Entities section's "still arriving, complete, or failed" status language? [Consistency, Spec §Key Entities]
- [ ] CHK013 Is the offline-cache scope in FR-011 ("every previously-opened conversation") fully reconciled with the Edge Cases statement about a never-opened conversation, leaving no undefined partially-cached state in between? [Consistency, Spec §FR-011]
- [ ] CHK014 Is "Novo Chat"'s behavior while offline (FR-009) consistent with FR-010's lazy-creation model and FR-012's block-on-offline rule, or does the spec leave an implicit third case unaddressed? [Consistency, Spec §FR-009/§FR-010/§FR-012]

## Acceptance Criteria Quality

- [ ] CHK015 Can SC-001's "100% of tested cases" be objectively verified without a documented minimum sample size or seeding procedure? [Measurability, Spec §SC-001]
- [ ] CHK016 Is SC-004's "zero observed duplicates" across "repeated retries" measurable without the spec specifying how many repeated retries constitute a sufficient test? [Measurability, Spec §SC-004]
- [ ] CHK017 Does SC-006's "re-enabling within one interaction of connectivity returning" define what counts as "one interaction" precisely enough to be testable (e.g., does a passive reconnect count, or only a user-initiated retry)? [Measurability, Spec §SC-006]
- [ ] CHK018 Does SC-007 define a specific session-count threshold used to verify "remains reachable by scrolling," or is the test condition left to the reviewer's discretion? [Measurability, Spec §SC-007]

## Scenario Coverage

- [ ] CHK019 Are requirements defined for retrying a message that failed mid-stream (partial text present) versus one that failed before any token arrived — is the retry-triggering UI treatment specified as identical in both cases? [Coverage, Spec §FR-006]
- [ ] CHK020 Is single-flight gating (FR-007) explicitly scoped to "per conversation," with a requirement covering whether a user can send in a different, idle conversation while another conversation's response is still in flight? [Clarity/Gap, Spec §FR-007]
- [ ] CHK021 Are requirements defined for retrying a message that is no longer in the error state by the time the retry call resolves (e.g., state changed via another device or session)? [Gap, Edge Cases]
- [ ] CHK022 Are requirements defined for the account's very-first-ever message, where no session yet exists and the RAG-grounding context (User Story 1) has no prior entries at all to draw on? [Coverage, Spec §Assumptions]

## Edge Case Coverage

- [ ] CHK023 Is there a requirement for connectivity dropping and returning more than once while a single response is still streaming? [Gap, Edge Cases]
- [ ] CHK024 Are requirements defined for cache staleness — if a cached session's history could diverge from the backend once connectivity returns, is a refresh required, or is the cache treated as authoritative until the user reopens the session? [Gap, Spec §FR-011]
- [ ] CHK025 Is the side menu's pagination requirement (FR-008) explicit about behavior when a cursor-paginated fetch fails mid-scroll (retry automatically, inline error, or silent stop)? [Gap, Spec §FR-008]
- [ ] CHK026 Is behavior specified for the app being backgrounded mid-stream and resumed — does the requirement rely solely on the existing "reflects whatever the backend ultimately recorded" rule (Edge Cases), or is a distinct resume/reconnect case needed? [Gap, Edge Cases]

## Non-Functional Requirements

- [ ] CHK027 Are performance expectations defined for the optimistic local message appearing after tap-to-send, distinct from the network-dependent streaming latency that follows it? [Completeness, Spec §Assumptions, Plan Performance Goals]
- [ ] CHK028 Are accessibility requirements (e.g., assistive-technology announcement of streaming → complete/error transitions) defined for chat message state changes? [Gap, Coverage]
- [ ] CHK029 Are requirements defined for how the session-expiration overlay (FR-013) interacts with an in-progress SSE stream specifically, beyond the general "history and scroll position preserved" statement already covering static views? [Completeness, Spec §FR-013]

## Dependencies & Assumptions

- [ ] CHK030 Is the assumption that "a session always has a `lastUserMessageAt` by the time it is listed" (Clarification 2) validated against the lazy-creation flow's actual ordering of session-creation and first-message-send calls? [Assumption, Spec Clarification 2]
- [ ] CHK031 Is the dependency on RF03/RF07's existing "Sessão expirada" overlay (FR-013) validated to already cover expiry occurring specifically mid-SSE-stream, not only during static history viewing? [Assumption, Spec §FR-013]
- [ ] CHK032 Is the assumption that chat's write-call error presentation "follows the same retryable/non-retryable pattern already established project-wide (RNF09)" validated against SSE-specific failure modes, such as a stream erroring after partial tokens were already delivered? [Assumption, Spec §Assumptions]

## Ambiguities & Conflicts

- [ ] CHK033 Does the spec bound how much or which prior content counts as "relevant" for grounding (User Story 1), or is relevance entirely opaque to the client with no observable contract? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-001]
- [ ] CHK034 Does the spec clarify whether a response that found no relevant prior entries is client-distinguishable from a grounded one, given FR-001's "MUST be able to reflect" language implies grounding is not guaranteed on every response? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-001]
- [ ] CHK035 Is "chat messages are conversational only" (FR-003) explicit about whether it excludes only entry-creation, or also other automatic side effects (e.g., analytics, proactive-insight triggers) not otherwise named in this unit's scope? [Clarity, Spec §FR-003]

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied
- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation
- `/speckit-implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers
- `checklists/requirements.md` has a separate built-in lifecycle maintained by `/speckit-specify` and `/speckit-clarify`
- Add comments or findings inline
- Link to relevant resources or documentation
- Items are numbered sequentially for easy reference

# Tasks: P-RF04 — Interactive chat with memory (RAG)

**Input**: Design documents from `/specs/007-chat-memory-rag/`
**Prerequisites**: plan.md, spec.md, research.md, data-model.md, contracts/, quickstart.md (all present)

**Tests**: Included. `plan.md`'s Constitution Check marks RNF07 (domain coverage ≥80%) and RNF09 (Either +
15/15 error scenarios) both "PASS (gate carried into tasks)", and every file under `contracts/` carries its own
"Test scenarios this contract owns" table plus `quickstart.md`'s "Automated checks" section — this is this
feature's own design material requesting test tasks, not an invented addition.

**Organization**: Tasks are grouped by user story (spec.md's five User Stories: P1, P1, P2, P2, P3). This
feature introduces one entirely new feature folder (`lib/features/chat/`, two blocs) plus two `core/network/`
extensions. Loading a conversation (resume-last / switch / new-empty) is needed by every single story — even
US4's "Novo Chat" and US5's offline browsing go through the same `_loadSession` path — so the shared
transport/data/repository layer and `ChatBloc`'s own "load a conversation" machinery are necessarily
Foundational; each User Story phase then adds that story's own handler bodies, widgets, and tests on top.

## Path Conventions

Single Flutter project (plan.md's "Project Type"): `lib/features/chat/{domain,data,presentation}/`, mirrored
under `test/features/chat/...`; two `core/network/` files extended in place; `lib/features/home/` extended in
place. No `backend/`/`frontend/` split, no `.env`/native project file touched, no change to
`docs/input/backend/api/openapi.yaml` (Constraints, FR-014).

---

## Phase 1: Setup

No setup tasks. `plan.md`'s "Primary Dependencies" is explicit — "No additions... reuses the full existing
stack" — and the Project Structure's "Structure Decision" already fixes every new file's location. Proceed
directly to Foundational.

---

## Phase 2: Foundational (Blocking Prerequisites)

**Purpose**: the shared transport (`SseFrame`/`ApiClient.sseStream`, live connectivity), the domain entities,
the data layer (`ChatRemoteDataSource`/`ChatLocalCache`/`ChatRepositoryImpl`), and `ChatBloc`'s own
"resume/switch/new empty conversation" machinery (`ChatStarted`/`ConversationSelected`/
`NewConversationRequested`/`_loadSession`) that every user story's handlers build on top of.

**⚠️ CRITICAL**: No user story phase can begin until this phase is complete.

- [X] T001 [P] Create `lib/core/network/sse_frame.dart`: `class SseFrame extends Equatable` with `final String
  event` and `final String data` (raw JSON text, parsed by the caller — `ApiClient` itself stays generic),
  `props => [event, data]` (data-model.md, contracts/sse-transport-extension.md).

- [X] T002 Extend `lib/core/network/api_client.dart` with `Stream<Either<Failure, SseFrame>> sseStream(String
  function, {required String method, Map<String, dynamic>? body, List<String>? pathSegments, AuthMode authMode
  = AuthMode.userSession})` per contracts/sse-transport-extension.md: issues the request via
  `_dio.request<ResponseBody>(url, options: Options(method: ..., responseType: ResponseType.stream, headers:
  {'apikey': _anonKey, 'Authorization': 'Bearer $bearer'}))` (same header-building logic `call()` already
  uses); decodes each byte chunk as UTF-8 (`allowMalformed: true`) into a buffer and splits frames on the
  blank-line (`\n\n`) SSE delimiter, parsing `event:`/`data:` lines per frame (multiple consecutive `data:`
  lines joined with `\n`; any other SSE field ignored); yields `Right(SseFrame(...))` per parsed frame in
  arrival order; on `DioException`, yields **exactly one** `Left(_mapException(e))` — reusing the existing
  `_mapException` verbatim, no second failure-mapping implementation — as the stream's **last** item, then the
  stream closes (no further iteration of `response.data!.stream` after the exception). `call()` is unchanged.
  Depends on T001.

- [X] T003 Create `test/core/network/api_client_sse_test.dart` per contracts/sse-transport-extension.md's "Test
  scenarios this contract owns" table: scenario #1 (3 frames split across 2 byte chunks mid-frame — all 3 parsed
  correctly, no dropped/duplicated bytes across the boundary); #2 (a `DioException` with `type: connectionTimeout`
  thrown after 1 frame already yielded — exactly `Right(frame1)` then `Left(NetworkTimeoutFailure)` as the
  stream's last item); #3 (a `DioException` with no `response` at all — `Left(NetworkOfflineFailure)` as the
  final item); #4 (a frame containing only `event: context\ndata: {}` — yielded as an ordinary
  `Right(SseFrame(event: 'context', data: '{}'))`, since the generic transport never special-cases an event
  name); #5 (a multi-line `data:` field split across two consecutive `data:` lines — both joined with `\n` into
  one `SseFrame.data`). Mock the underlying `dio` stream response the same way `api_client_test.dart`'s existing
  `call()` tests already mock `Dio`. Depends on T002.

- [X] T004 [P] Add `Stream<bool> get onConnectivityChanged` to `lib/core/network/connectivity_checker.dart`
  (research.md R8): wraps `Connectivity().onConnectivityChanged`'s own broadcast stream, mapping "any result
  `!= ConnectivityResult.none`" → `true` — the exact same predicate `hasConnection()` already uses. The existing
  synchronous `hasConnection()` method is unchanged (R8's own write-path pre-check still calls it directly).

- [X] T005 [P] Create `lib/features/chat/domain/entities/chat_session.dart`: `enum ChatPersona { analitico,
  empatico, socratico }`; `class ChatSession extends Equatable` with `required` fields `id` (`String`), `title`
  (`String`), `personaSnapshot` (`ChatPersona` — read-only here, FR-014, never written back), `userMessageCount`
  (`int`), `lastUserMessageAt` (`DateTime?` — "nullable per schema; in practice always non-null once listed"),
  `createdAt`/`updatedAt` (`DateTime`); `props` over all seven fields (data-model.md).

- [X] T006 [P] Create `lib/features/chat/domain/entities/chat_message.dart`: `enum ChatRole { user, assistant
  }`; `enum ChatMessageStatus { streaming, complete, failed }`; `class ChatMessage extends Equatable` with
  `required` fields `id` (`String` — `'local-<timestamp>'`-prefixed until reconciled with the server's real id,

  (`int`), `status`, `retryCount` (`int`), `createdAt`; `bool get isOptimistic => id.startsWith('local-')`;
  `props` over `[id, sessionId, role, content, seq, status, retryCount, createdAt]` (data-model.md).

- [X] T007 [P] Create `lib/features/chat/domain/entities/chat_sessions_page.dart`: `class ChatSessionsPage
  extends Equatable` with `final List<ChatSession> sessions` and `final String? nextCursor` (`meta.nextCursor`
  verbatim; `null` = last page) — directly mirrors `EntriesPage`'s own shape. Depends on T005.

- [X] T008 [P] Create `lib/features/chat/domain/entities/chat_stream_event.dart`: `sealed class ChatStreamEvent
  extends Equatable`; `MessageCreated({required String userMessageId, required String assistantMessageId})`;
  `ContextReceived()` (no fields); `TokenReceived(String delta)`; `StreamDone({required String

  `Stream<Either<Failure, ChatStreamEvent>>` (data-model.md, research.md R2).

- [X] T009 [P] Create `lib/features/chat/domain/entities/chat_title_deriver.dart`: `class ChatTitleDeriver`
  with a private constructor, `static const _maxLength = 48`, and `static String derive(String
  firstMessageText)` — collapses internal whitespace/newlines to single spaces via `replaceAll(RegExp(r'\s+'),
  ' ')`, trims, and when the result's length exceeds 48 returns `'${collapsed.substring(0, 48)}…'`, otherwise
  the collapsed string unchanged. Pure, total; never returns an empty string for non-empty input; no
  `package:flutter` import, no I/O (research.md R6, Principle V).

- [X] T010 Create `lib/features/chat/domain/repositories/chat_repository.dart`: abstract `ChatRepository` with
  `Future<Either<Failure, ChatSession>> createSession({required String title})`; `Future<Either<Failure,
  ChatSessionsPage>> listSessions({String? cursor, int? limit})`; `List<ChatSession> get cachedSessions`;
  `Future<Either<Failure, List<ChatMessage>>> listMessages(String sessionId)`; `List<ChatMessage>?
  cachedMessages(String sessionId)` (`null` = this session's history was never fetched while online); `Future<void>
  setLastActiveSessionId(String? sessionId)`; `Future<String?> get lastActiveSessionId`; `Stream<Either<Failure,
  ChatStreamEvent>> sendMessage({required String sessionId, required String content})`;
  `Stream<Either<Failure, ChatStreamEvent>> retryMessage({required String sessionId, required String
  userMessageId})` — exactly data-model.md's interface. Depends on T005, T006, T007, T008.

- [X] T011 [P] Create `lib/features/chat/data/chat_local_cache.dart` (research.md R4): Keychain-backed
  (`FlutterSecureStorage`, JSON-encoded, same pattern `EntriesLocalCache` already establishes), three
  **independent** storage keys so one write never clobbers another — `chatSessionsLocalCache` (a JSON array,
  upsert-by-id merge — `readSessions()`/`writeSessions(List<ChatSession>)`), `chatMessagesLocalCache` (a JSON
  object keyed by `sessionId`, replace-whole-list-per-session since `chat-messages-list` always returns the

  JSON string, or the key absent when no session exists yet — `readLastActiveSessionId()`/
  `writeLastActiveSessionId(String? sessionId)`). Depends on T005, T006.

## Dependencies & Execution Order

### Phase Dependencies

- **Foundational (Phase 2)**: no dependencies — can start immediately. **BLOCKS** every user story phase (every
  story needs `ChatBloc`'s "load a conversation" machinery at minimum).
- **User Story 1 (Phase 3)**: depends on Foundational only. MVP.
- **User Story 2 (Phase 4)**: depends on Foundational **and** US1's `_consumeTurn` (T022) — its failure-handling
  branch is built as part of that same function and cannot be split; this phase is otherwise test-only.
- **User Story 3 (Phase 5)**: depends on Foundational and US1's `_consumeTurn` (T022), which it reuses verbatim
  for the retry's own stream consumption.
- **User Story 4 (Phase 6)**: depends on Foundational only — independent of US1/US2/US3's own tasks (no shared
  code with `ChatBloc`'s turn-consumption machinery).
- **User Story 5 (Phase 7)**: depends on Foundational's `_loadSession`/`ChatSessionsBloc` cache-fallback logic
  (already built there) and on `ChatComposer` (T023, US1) for its own offline-disabling test.
- **Polish (Phase 8)**: depends on all five user stories being complete.

### Within Each Phase

- Tasks touching the *same* file (`chat_bloc.dart`, `home_chat_shell_page.dart`, `app_drawer.dart`,
  `service_locator.dart`, `app_router.dart`) are listed in the sequential order they must be applied.
- Tasks creating a *new* file with no dependency on that phase's other new files are marked `[P]`.
- Test tasks are marked `[P]` relative to each other (distinct test files); each still depends on its
  corresponding implementation task(s) existing to pass.

### Parallel Opportunities

- T001, T004–T009, T014, T015, T017 (Foundational's entities/events/states/widgets/transport) can all run in
  parallel — ten independent files with no cross-dependencies among them.
- T011 and T012 (local cache, remote data source) can run in parallel with each other once T001–T009 land.
- All test tasks within a single user story phase can run in parallel with each other.
- User Story 4 (side menu) can be implemented in parallel with User Stories 1–3 (the live conversation) by a
  second developer, since neither `ChatSessionsBloc` nor `AppDrawer`'s "CONVERSAS" section shares any code path
  with `ChatBloc`'s turn-consumption machinery.

## Implementation Strategy

### MVP First (User Story 1 Only)

1. Complete Phase 2: Foundational (transport, data layer, entities, `ChatBloc`'s conversation-loading core).
2. Complete Phase 3: User Story 1 (lazy session creation, send, stream, persist, no entry created).
3. **STOP and VALIDATE**: seed a prior entry, send a related message, confirm the grounded response (SC-001);
   restart the app and confirm the exchange persists (SC-005).
4. Demo/ship if ready — this alone delivers RF04's "entire premise" (spec.md, User Story 1's "Why this
   priority").

### Incremental Delivery

1. Foundational → User Story 1 (MVP: grounded, persisted conversation).
2. + User Story 2 (the three-state visual contract — mostly tests over already-built engine behavior).
3. + User Story 3 (tap-to-retry on a failed response).
4. + User Story 4 (side menu: list, paginate, "Novo Chat") — independently buildable in parallel with 2–3.
5. + User Story 5 (offline banner + multi-conversation offline coverage).
6. + Polish (verification gates, manual walkthrough).

Each stage adds value without breaking the previous one, matching spec.md's own stated priority order (P1, P1,
P2, P2, P3).

1	# Quickstart: P-RF04 — Interactive chat with memory (RAG)
2	
3	How to validate this unit end-to-end once implemented, mapped to spec.md's five user stories. A run guide —
4	interfaces are in `contracts/`, state/entities in `data-model.md`.
5	
6	## Prerequisites
7	
8	- F000 and RF03 (vault/auth) already implemented and passing — a signed-in, authenticated test account can
9	  reach `/home`.
10	- At least one prior entry seeded on the test account about a specific, identifiable topic (reuse
11	  `docs/input/backend/fixtures/seeded-search-entries.md`'s own fixtures if the backend's RAG retrieval draws
12	  from the same entries RF06 already seeds) — needed for Story 1's "grounded in your own journal" check.
13	- An account with zero chat sessions yet, for the Edge Case "first-ever use of chat" scenario, and a second
14	  account (or the same account after Story 1) with 2+ sessions and, ideally, more sessions than
15	  `chat-sessions-list`'s default page `limit` (20) for the SC-007 pagination check.
16	- A way to force a mid-stream connection drop or backend error for Story 2/3 (airplane mode toggled partway
17	  through a response, or a test double at the repository layer for automated tests).
18	
19	## Automated checks
20	
21	```bash
22	fvm flutter analyze                                    # RNF06 import-shape lint
23	fvm flutter test --coverage
24	lcov --extract coverage/lcov.info 'lib/**/domain/**' -o coverage/domain.info
25	genhtml coverage/domain.info -o coverage/domain-html    # RNF07 gate — ChatTitleDeriver, ChatStreamEvent,
26	                                                         # ChatMessage's status-transition logic, etc.
27	dart test/architecture/no_bloc_imports_bloc_test.dart   # ChatBloc/ChatSessionsBloc stay within lib/features/chat/
28	dart test/architecture/domain_purity_test.dart          # chat/domain/ imports neither Flutter nor chat/data/
29	```
30	
31	`contracts/sse-transport-extension.md`, `contracts/chat-repository.md`, `contracts/chat-bloc.md`, and
32	`contracts/chat-sessions-bloc.md` each carry the full scenario table this unit's coverage depends on.
33	
34	## Manual verification (device/Simulator)
35	
36	### Story 1 — Getting an answer grounded in your own journal (P1)
37	
38	1. With the seeded prior entry present, open the chat and send a message related to that entry's topic
39	   without quoting it (e.g., if the entry is about pre-presentation anxiety, ask "o que me ajuda a lidar com
40	   nervosismo antes de falar em público?"). **Expect**: the streamed response reflects the seeded entry's
41	   content (SC-001).
42	2. Leave the chat screen (open "Meus Registros", then come back via the side menu), then fully restart the
43	   app. **Expect**: the full exchange, in the same order, is still present with no resend (Acceptance
44	   Scenario 2).
45	3. Open "Meus Registros" right after sending a chat message. **Expect**: no new entry was created from it —
46	   the chat message exists only in the conversation, never as a journal entry (Acceptance Scenario 3/FR-003).
47	
48	### Story 2 — Always knowing what the agent is doing (P1)
49	
50	1. Send a message. **Expect**: the response appears progressively with a visible streaming indicator
51	   (pulsing cursor), distinct from a finished bubble.
52	2. Let it finish normally. **Expect**: the final text is shown with a timestamp, no streaming indicator left
53	   (Acceptance Scenario 2).
54	3. Send another message, then force a mid-stream failure (airplane mode, or kill the backend connection).
55	   **Expect**: whatever partial text had already arrived stays visible, with "Falha ao gerar resposta" in
56	   place of the timestamp — never blanked or removed (SC-003).
57	
58	### Story 3 — Recovering from a failed response without losing the conversation (P2)
59	
60	1. On the failed message from Story 2, tap it. **Expect**: a fresh attempt starts, going through the same
61	   streaming → complete/error states; the original question still appears exactly once in the history
62	   (SC-004).
63	2. Force the retry itself to fail again. **Expect**: the same failure state, with the same tap-to-retry
64	   affordance — not a dead end (Acceptance Scenario 3).
65	3. Scroll up to an older failed message (not the most recent one in the conversation) and retry it. **Expect**:
66	   only that message's response changes; every later message is untouched (Edge Cases).
67	
68	### Story 4 — Organizing conversations from the side menu (P2)
69	
70	1. With at least one existing conversation, open the side menu (☰). **Expect**: a "CONVERSAS" section lists
71	   each conversation with a title (derived from its first message) and a timestamp, most-recently-active
72	   first.
73	2. Tap "Novo Chat". **Expect**: the chat screen shows an empty conversation, composer ready; the previous
74	   conversation is unaffected (Acceptance Scenario 2).
75	3. Send a first message in this new conversation, then reopen the side menu. **Expect**: the new conversation
76	   now appears in "CONVERSAS" with its derived title (research.md R6).
77	4. Tap the earlier conversation from the list. **Expect**: its full history reopens exactly as it was left
78	   (Acceptance Scenario 3).
79	5. On an account with more sessions than one backend page, scroll to the bottom of "CONVERSAS". **Expect**:
80	   the next page loads via `cursor`, with no conversation ever permanently hidden (SC-007).
81	
82	### Story 5 — Reading history while offline (P3)
83	
84	1. With a conversation already loaded, enable airplane mode. **Expect**: the existing history stays visible
85	   and scrollable; a banner explains new messages are blocked; the composer's send control is visibly
86	   disabled.
87	2. Try to type and send anyway. **Expect**: nothing is sent — the control stays disabled, no request is
88	   attempted (FR-012).
89	3. While still offline, open the side menu and switch to a *different* conversation that was opened at least
90	   once earlier while online. **Expect**: its own cached history shows correctly too — not just the
91	   conversation that happened to be open when connectivity dropped (SC-006/Clarification 3).
92	4. While still offline, select from the side menu a conversation that has **never** been opened before.
93	   **Expect**: the standard no-connection state appears instead of any content (Edge Cases) — distinct from
94	   the normal "cached and readable" case in step 3.
95	5. Disable airplane mode. **Expect**: the send control re-enables and the offline banner disappears without
96	   any manual action, within one interaction (SC-006).
97	
98	### Edge cases worth exercising manually at least once
99	
100	- Try to send an empty or whitespace-only message. **Expect**: the send control stays disabled; no request
101	  fires.
102	- Type a message at the 8000-character cap (`chat.messages.send`'s `maxLength`). **Expect**: the field simply
103	  stops accepting further characters — no backend validation round-trip is ever needed (research.md R12).
104	- Send a message, then immediately try to send another before the first response resolves. **Expect**: the
105	  composer stays disabled for the whole conversation until that turn completes or is retried to a new
106	  resolution (FR-007).
107	- Force a session expiration ("Sessão expirada") while a response is mid-stream. **Expect**: the existing
108	  overlay appears, history and scroll position are preserved underneath it, and re-authenticating resumes the
109	  same conversation exactly where it was (Edge Cases — reusing RF03/RF07's existing behavior, not a new one).
110	- Navigate away from a conversation (via the side menu) while a response is still streaming, then return to
111	  it a few seconds later. **Expect**: the message reflects whatever the backend ultimately recorded (complete
112	  or failed), not a stuck in-progress state (Edge Cases; research.md R11).
113	- On a brand-new account with zero conversations, open the chat screen. **Expect**: an empty, ready-to-send
114	  conversation is shown immediately — no session is created until the first message is actually sent
115	  (Edge Cases/FR-010).

   **Expect**: whatever partial text had already arrived stays visible, with "Falha ao gerar resposta" in
   place of the timestamp — never blanked or removed (SC-003).

### Story 3 — Recovering from a failed response without losing the conversation (P2)

1. On the failed message from Story 2, tap it. **Expect**: a fresh attempt starts, going through the same
   streaming → complete/error states; the original question still appears exactly once in the history
   (SC-004).
2. Force the retry itself to fail again. **Expect**: the same failure state, with the same tap-to-retry
   affordance — not a dead end (Acceptance Scenario 3).
3. Scroll up to an older failed message (not the most recent one in the conversation) and retry it. **Expect**:
   only that message's response changes; every later message is untouched (Edge Cases).

### Story 4 — Organizing conversations from the side menu (P2)

1. With at least one existing conversation, open the side menu (☰). **Expect**: a "CONVERSAS" section lists
   each conversation with a title (derived from its first message) and a timestamp, most-recently-active
   first.
2. Tap "Novo Chat". **Expect**: the chat screen shows an empty conversation, composer ready; the previous
   conversation is unaffected (Acceptance Scenario 2).
3. Send a first message in this new conversation, then reopen the side menu. **Expect**: the new conversation
   now appears in "CONVERSAS" with its derived title (research.md R6).
4. Tap the earlier conversation from the list. **Expect**: its full history reopens exactly as it was left
   (Acceptance Scenario 3).
5. On an account with more sessions than one backend page, scroll to the bottom of "CONVERSAS". **Expect**:
   the next page loads via `cursor`, with no conversation ever permanently hidden (SC-007).

### Story 5 — Reading history while offline (P3)

1. With a conversation already loaded, enable airplane mode. **Expect**: the existing history stays visible
   and scrollable; a banner explains new messages are blocked; the composer's send control is visibly
   disabled.
2. Try to type and send anyway. **Expect**: nothing is sent — the control stays disabled, no request is
   attempted (FR-012).
3. While still offline, open the side menu and switch to a *different* conversation that was opened at least
   once earlier while online. **Expect**: its own cached history shows correctly too — not just the
   conversation that happened to be open when connectivity dropped (SC-006/Clarification 3).
4. While still offline, select from the side menu a conversation that has **never** been opened before.
   **Expect**: the standard no-connection state appears instead of any content (Edge Cases) — distinct from
   the normal "cached and readable" case in step 3.
5. Disable airplane mode. **Expect**: the send control re-enables and the offline banner disappears without
   any manual action, within one interaction (SC-006).

### Edge cases worth exercising manually at least once

- Try to send an empty or whitespace-only message. **Expect**: the send control stays disabled; no request
  fires.
- Type a message at the 8000-character cap (`chat.messages.send`'s `maxLength`). **Expect**: the field simply
  stops accepting further characters — no backend validation round-trip is ever needed (research.md R12).
- Send a message, then immediately try to send another before the first response resolves. **Expect**: the
  composer stays disabled for the whole conversation until that turn completes or is retried to a new
  resolution (FR-007).
- Force a session expiration ("Sessão expirada") while a response is mid-stream. **Expect**: the existing
  overlay appears, history and scroll position are preserved underneath it, and re-authenticating resumes the
  same conversation exactly where it was (Edge Cases — reusing RF03/RF07's existing behavior, not a new one).
- Navigate away from a conversation (via the side menu) while a response is still streaming, then return to
  it a few seconds later. **Expect**: the message reflects whatever the backend ultimately recorded (complete
  or failed), not a stuck in-progress state (Edge Cases; research.md R11).
- On a brand-new account with zero conversations, open the chat screen. **Expect**: an empty, ready-to-send
  conversation is shown immediately — no session is created until the first message is actually sent
  (Edge Cases/FR-010).
